items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: was a trumpet player who was with me for 18 years, even in my Chicago band

ctx.x: enough. I used to go down and stand down and watch these things. They said, you want to see guys go upstairs and come out with -- guys used to stand on the street sometime with a trumpet, saxophone, and fiddle. Violin, you know. (Inaudible) Waitin' for -- all gigs in New York. (unintelligible). Then you go to the Metropole, and you know the story of the Metropole. But getting back to a mixed group. We had quite a few fellas that would frequent Minton's, and I used to use a lot of mixed guys, a lot of them -- I…

I would mention that was in that seven piece group -- we're talking in the forties now -- was a trumpet player who was with me for 18 years, even in my Chicago band, and he just died recently -- Gayle Brockman was his name. I'll tell you. I know you'll know him. He's the guy that played the original trumpet solo with Jug. Jug is Gene Ammonds.
